1.support: Our purposes were to assess Pes-guided strategy to set PEEP in SP and in PP as compared with a PEEP/FIO2 table and to explore the early (1 h) and late (16 h) effects of PP on lung and chest wall mechanics.

2.support: Adult ARDS patients with PaO2/FIO2 ≤ 150 mmHg under invasive mechanical ventilation including PEEP ≥ 5 cmH2O and VT = 6 mL/kg predicted body weight were included in two academic medical intensive care units (Additional file 1: Figure S1).
2.location: Page 2, Methods, Study design and population

3.support: From January 1, 2016, to March 31, 2017, 38 patients (27 male) were enrolled (Additional file 1: Table S1 and Figure S1).

4.support: The report does not state how many patients were screened or whether every patient meeting the entry criteria was enrolled; the flow chart cited (Additional file 1: Figure S1) is not printed in the article.
4.location: Page 3, Results, Patients; page 2, Methods, Study design and population

5.support: Sample size was computed to 28 based on primary endpoint (Pes,ee) [24]. To account for incomplete data, we planned to include 38 patients.

6.support: Supine head-up at 30° at Pes-guided PEEP. PEEP was titrated by 1 cmH2O-steps to reach PL,ee of 3 ± 2 cmH2O.
6.location: Page 2, Protocol, step 2; steps 1–4 also on page 3

7.support: Pes and gastric pressure (Pga) were recorded with Nutrivent device (Sidam, Italy) after verification of correct placement [19] and non-stress minimal volume implementation [20].
7.location: Page 2, Methods, Measurements; page 3, Measurements and Fig. 1

8.support: The report does not describe any blinding of the personnel assessing outcomes, and the investigators who set the PEEP strategy and performed the measurements necessarily knew the PEEP level and the patient's position.

9.support: All the data were lacking for Pes-guided PEEP in SP in one patient, who required immediate PP, and in late prone in 2 patients (1 death and 1 patient returned in SP for urgent coronarography).

10.support: Data were compared by repeated measures 2-factor ANOVA. Categorical variables were compared using chi-squared test.
10.location: Page 3, Statistical analysis; p values for before-after contrasts in Tables 1–3 (pages 4 and 7)

11.support: I looked for repeated measurements of the outcomes before and after the intervention; the report states that for each protocol step measurements were done once, 1 h after the PEEP change, and does not describe an interrupted time-series design.

12.support: PEEP titration with an esophageal balloon was applied to individual patients in this before-after physiologic study; the report describes no group-level (unit, hospital or community) allocation or intervention.

nih.rationale: Rated Fair. The question, eligibility criteria, intervention (PEEP titrated in 1 cmH2O steps to a PL,ee target of 3 ± 2 cmH2O) and the objective, machine-derived outcome measurements are all clearly described, a sample size calculation is reported, and pre-post changes are tested with p values given (items 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10). The study falls short of Good because outcome assessors were not blinded (item 8 = No), because outcomes were measured only once at each step rather than by an interrupted time-series design (item 11 = No), because it is not reported how many eligible patients were enrolled (item 4 = NR), and because EIT data were missing in 11 of 38 patients (29%). It is not Poor: the main mechanics, gas exchange and EELV data were complete in 36–37 of 38 patients with reasons for the losses given, the measurements are objective and obtained with validated, described technique, and the authors acknowledge the non-randomised early application of PEEP strategy and the possible carry-over effect.
